end.summary: Named examples of plant-eaters, meat-eaters, and animals that eat both; gave reasons for the examples. Practised building food chains; some chains were in the right order, but this is not steady yet. Practised that plants make food using sunlight and water; easy questions were answered, but a why or new-situation question is still needed. Practised predicting changes when a chain member is removed; some predictions were right, but this is not steady yet. An early food-chain order mix-up was corrected later, and the arrow direction was linked to who eats whom.
end.parentNote: Manav practised classifying animals by what they eat, building food chains, explaining that plants make their own food, and predicting changes when one part is removed. They used reasons such as “the grasshopper eats grass” and connected arrows to the eater; an early chain-order mix-up was corrected later in the lesson. At home, ask them to build two new food chains with picture cards and explain each arrow, then ask what might happen if one part disappeared.
